note: What the City's budget covers, and what it doesn't (#51): the Sources page's 'What this budget covers' block and the overview's property-tax line. Sources added here are other governments' documents and explainers, never the City's own books; they continue the documents' numbering. The City's own adopted budget (S1) is cited where it says the thing itself. Every quote must appear on its page of source/excerpts/{source}.json (page 1 for a web page). Text can name {allFunds}, {generalFund}, {propertyTax} and {year}, which the pages fill from budget.json with their receipts, and link [words](glossary:Term) or [words](a source's URL). Any other number in a paragraph must appear in one of its cites' quotes. A paragraph with no cites says why in 'unsourced'. FUSD's budget page links its 2026-27 budget report as a Google Drive file; the report's cover reads 'Proposed Budget', and its certification page gives the June 24, 2026 adoption date.

glossary.definition: A tax set at a fixed amount for each parcel of property (or for each room or square foot). A local government needs two-thirds of voters to approve one.
glossary.quote: With the approval of two-thirds of voters, local governments may impose a tax on all parcels in their jurisdiction (or a subset of parcels in their jurisdiction). Local governments typically set parcel taxes at fixed amounts per parcel (or fixed amounts per room or per square foot of the parcel).

glossary.definition: A separate local government that runs public schools. Fremont Unified School District is governed by a five-member Board of Education, each member elected to a four-year term.
glossary.quote: The District is governed by a five-member Board of Education. Each member is elected to a four-year term.

glossary.definition: A local government set up to provide a particular service in its area, such as fire protection, water, or parks and recreation. Special districts get a share of the 1% property tax, along with counties, cities and schools.
glossary.quote: property tax revenue from the 1 percent rate is distributed to counties, cities, K-12 schools, community college districts, and special districts

questions.question: Is this everything the City of Fremont spends?

Public schools in Fremont are run by Fremont Unified School District (FUSD), a separate government. It is governed by a five-member Board of Education, each member elected to a four-year term.

questions.question: Where does my property tax go?

paragraphs.text: The basic 1% property tax is pooled by the county and divided under state law among the county, cities, schools and [special districts](glossary:Special District).

cites.quote: Your county auditor pools your 1 percent rate tax payment, as well as payments from other property owners in your county, into a single countywide pot.
State law directs how your county auditor distributes the revenue in the countywide pot.
your county auditor sets aside this $1,000 for your city, county, schools, and special districts.

paragraphs.text: The City says it receives about 15 cents of every dollar of property tax paid, and that Alameda County and the schools, including FUSD, receive most of it.

cites.quote: The City of Fremont receives approximately 15 cents of every dollar of property tax paid. Alameda County and the schools, including Fremont Unified School District, receive most of the revenue from property taxes assessed on property located in the City

paragraphs.text: The {propertyTax} in property tax on these pages is only the City's share.

questions.question: Does the City pay for the schools?

paragraphs.text: FUSD's budget groups its General Fund money by kind: the state's school funding formula (LCFF), federal revenue, other state revenue and other local revenue. The state formula is by far the largest.

3) Other State Revenue 8300-8599
4) Other Local Revenue 8600-8799

paragraphs.text: The City's own budget describes joint work with the district, such as a recycling coordinator funding agreement and police School Resource Officers who partner with FUSD.

The School Resource Officer (SRO) Unit will continue to partner with the Fremont Unified School District to deliver professional public safety and services.
